say: A producer has seconds to decide what goes on air, and one wrong number costs trust.
Studio Desk's agents, built on Microsoft Agent Framework and Foundry, find and explain the stories. Every number comes from code. Low-risk graphics air on their own; nothing risky airs without her.
They read the match through an MCP server that stops at the current minute. A big chance is a reading of the game, so it waits for her.
She types a number the facts don't support. The desk refuses it and logs it.
Behind the story, each number is a fact computed by code, with its source event.
One click swaps the code's line for the agents' own, and the audit log records both decisions.
One desk, four broadcasts at once: the same goal for an analyst, for kids, for an Ostwick fan in Italian and a casual fan in Spanish, all from the same facts.
Viewers can ask too: answers use only facts up to that minute, and Content Safety checks question and answer.
One switch takes every AI story off air; template graphics carry on. If an agent fails, fixed rules stand in. Traces show each step's cost.
Model calls cost six to ten cents a match. No model keys, everything in Bicep, tests on every push.
Agents also read the game: a change of shape waits for her, with its evidence. Next: Entra ID roles and a durable audit store.
